issues.description: Function name mismatch for the state-preparation routine: the problem statement (problem_statement.md) documents the function as `_construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(Hx: npt.NDArray[np.int8], offset: int=0) -> stim.Circuit` (leading underscore), while both the template (template_repository/msd.py) and the solution (solution_repository/msd.py) implement and export the function as `construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(...)` (no leading underscore). This inconsistency can confuse students about which name to implement and which name tests will call, and may cause import/test failures or wasted time reconciling the three artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. The least disruptive fix is to update problem_statement.md to refer to construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(...) (remove the leading underscore) so it matches the template and solution. Alternatively, if a leading-underscore name is intentional, rename the implementations in the template and solution to `_construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(...)` and update any tests. Ensure the tests and documentation use the same public name.
